text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> PD#8242: frontend inference latency-surge (prod) — triggered by p99 > 700ms across router cluster. Notifying on-call schedule.

pagerduty-bot: page sent to @maria (on-call). Escalation schedule: 5m -> sre-jamie -> ben if unacked.

maria: acked. looking at traces now. seeing spike from router-12 and router-15.

maria: no 5xxs from the inference service, mostly elevated downstream latency and 504s at the edge for a subset of long-sequence requests.

sre-jamie: thx — can you paste the top traces and a quick search for "kv_cache_miss"?

maria: quick tail from router logs: ```
2026-03-15T10:02:13Z router-12 route_request id=abc123 lat=920ms model=redwood-open-70b qlen=1024 kv_cache_hit=false
2026-03-15T10:02:14Z router-15 route_request id=def456 lat=880ms model=redwood-open-70b kv_cache_hit=false
```

maria: also seeing a flurry of long-context requests from a single client IP range, looks synthetic-ish.

sre-jamie: interesting — kv cache misses + long context -> expensive model execution. can we temporarily route that IP range to a lower-cost variant and enable prefix caching?

ben: I'm standing by to adjust routing rules. what region is affected?

maria: primarily us-east-1, a little in us-west-2.

ops-liz: re: routing change, suggest a safe rollout: 10% traffic to redwood-70b-q4 (quantized) as fallback, keep 90% to primary, monitor p95. will do a canary.

sre-jamie: agree. also bump router concurrency on router-12 from 256->384 for 5m to drain backlog.

maria: applying routing canary now: `infractl route update --match client_ip=203.0.113.0/24 --to redwood-70b-q4 --weight 10%`

maria: `infractl router scale --name router-12 --concurrency 384 --duration 5m`

eng-runtime-bot: autoscaler: router-12 concurrency increased (256 -> 384). new config applied in 4s.

maria: canary in place, watching metrics. p99 dropped from ~900ms -> 420ms for matched traffic. overall p99 is trending down.

sre-jamie: nice. any customer-facing errors? logs show 504s at edge before, are they clearing?

maria: error rate down to baseline for most customers. two enterprise customers saw degraded latencies (retries increased) — flagged to CSM. no SLA breaches yet.

ben: ack. i'll keep the routing canary at 10% for 10m then increment to 25% if stable. ping me if it re-escalates.

incident-bot: PagerDuty PD#8242 acknowledged by maria. escalation paused.

maria: holding for 8m to ensure no rebound. kv cache warmup kicking in — cache hit ratio up from 12% -> 78% for the affected prefix set.

ops-liz: can we add a short-lived prefix pre-warm for the rest of the cluster? script: ```bash
curl -X POST https://console.internal/prewarm -d '{"prefixes": ["/v1/generate/longcontext"], "ttl": 600}'
```

maria: running prewarm now.

eng-runtime-bot: prewarm job started (job id: prewarm-559). estimated duration 55s.

maria: prewarm finished, hit ratio stabilized. overall p99 now ~220ms.

sre-jamie: good mitigation. can we add a short note to PD and mark as "recovered - keep monitoring"?

maria: updating PD and closing the immediate page: "Transient latency spike driven by long-context synthetic traffic; mitigated via routing canary to quantized model, concurrency bump, and cache prewarm. No customer SLA violations detected. Monitoring continues."

pagerduty-bot: PD#8242 updated: status=acknowledged->resolved by maria.

incident-bot: Alert auto-resolve: metric p99 latency returned below threshold for 15m. Closing alert thread.

ben: taking over follow-up to create a runbook bullet: "if kv cache miss storm + long-context requests => route to quantized fallback + prewarm prefixes + short concurrency bump". i'll add it to the playbook.

maria: thanks — handing off to ben for post-incident notes.

ben: on it, will file a short post-mortem and tag eng-runtime + product if customers were affected.

maria: thanks all :thumbsup: feel free to re-open if anything re-appears.

incident-bot: thread closed (auto-resolved).
